about:
# LootToastMover

A small World of Warcraft addon that lets you move the loot toast alerts
(`AlertFrame`) anywhere on screen instead of leaving them in Blizzard's default
position near the top center. One download works in every version of the game Blizzard
runs: retail, World of Warcraft: Forever, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Classic Era,
TBC Anniversary and Titan Reforged Classic.

## What it does

Blizzard's alert system anchors loot toasts, achievement popups and similar alerts to a
fixed screen position managed by the UI's frame position manager. LootToastMover opts
`AlertFrame` out of that manager and re-anchors it to a draggable anchor box you position
yourself. The position is saved account-wide and reapplied on login.

## Installation

Install from CurseForge (project `1262382`), or grab the zip from the
[latest release](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/releases/latest) and
extract it into the `AddOns` folder of the game you play:

```
<World of Warcraft>/_retail_/Interface/AddOns/         # retail
<World of Warcraft>/_classic_/Interface/AddOns/        # Mists of Pandaria Classic
<World of Warcraft>/_classic_era_/Interface/AddOns/    # Classic Era
<World of Warcraft>/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/   # Forever beta
```

The other games each have a folder of their own alongside these, and the folder for
Forever's full launch on November 4 has not been announced. Whichever game it is, the addon
goes in the `Interface/AddOns/` folder inside that game's folder.

The release zip already contains a correctly named `LootToastMover/` folder. If you copy
from a git checkout instead, the folder **must** be named `LootToastMover` — the
repository directory name (`loot-toast-mover`) will not load.

The addon is two Lua files, its code and its translations, with no third-party
dependencies.

## Usage

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/ltm` | Show or hide the draggable anchor box |
| `/ltm test` | Show a sample loot toast |
| `/ltm reset` | Move the anchor back to its default position |
| `/ltm config` | Open the options panel |
| `/ltm minimap` | Show or hide the minimap button |

`/loottoastpos` is the original command and still works; `/ltm` is a shorter alias for it.

The anchor box is the toast's actual footprint — same 276×96 size as a real loot toast,
sitting exactly where the first one will appear. Drag it with the left mouse button and
what you see is where toasts land. Further toasts stack upward from it.

`/ltm test` fires a genuine loot toast through Blizzard's alert system, so you can confirm
the placement without waiting for a drop. Run `/ltm` again, or press Escape, to hide the box
when you are done.

The box also appears on its own while Edit Mode is open, next to the rest of your UI, and
goes when you close it.

Toasts stack upward from the box, as Blizzard's always have. If you keep the box near the
top of the screen, tick **Stack new toasts downward** in the options panel: the first toast
still lands on the box and the rest hang below it instead of running off the top.

## Where to find it

The same three actions are reachable from four places, so the addon is visible however your
UI is set up:

- **Minimap button** — the bag icon on the minimap ring. Left-click toggles the anchor box,
  right-click opens the options panel, and dragging moves the button around the ring. Show
  or hide it from the options panel or with `/ltm minimap`. A new install in retail or
  Forever starts with it hidden, because the Addon Compartment there already lists the
  addon; the Classic games show it.
- **Options panel** — Game Menu → Options → AddOns → **LootToastMover**, with buttons for
  everything the slash commands do. `/ltm config` opens it directly.
- **Broker plugin** — if you run a broker display (Titan Panel, Bazooka, ChocolateBar,
  ElvUI datatexts, …), LootToastMover appears in its plugin list as a launcher. Same clicks
  as the minimap button.
- **Addon Compartment** — the addon-list button next to the minimap. Retail and Forever
  only; the Classic games do not have one.

The broker plugin only appears when a broker display is installed. LibDataBroker is looked
up rather than bundled, because every broker bar ships its own copy; see
[Dependencies](#dependencies).

## Compatibility

One zip runs in every version of the game Blizzard currently runs. The TOC lists an
Interface number for each, and a client loads the addon as long as one of them is its own:

| Game | Interface | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retail (Midnight) | `120105`, `120100` | 12.1.5, 12.1.0 |
| World of Warcraft: Forever | `16001` | 1.60.1 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | `50504` | 5.5.4 |
| Titan Reforged Classic (China only) | `38002` | 3.80.2 |
| TBC Anniversary | `20506` | 2.5.6 |
| Classic Era | `11509` | 1.15.9 |

Retail lists two numbers while patch 12.1.5 rolls out. Regions patch on different days, so
for a while some clients are still on 12.1.0, and each needs its own number to load the
addon. The release workflow's Interface update writes one number per game, so the next one
drops `120100`.

[`tools/games.lua`](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/blob/main/tools/games.lua) is the same list in code; the TOC check and the
release tooling both work from it.

The addon needs no per-game code. Forever runs the retail client and UI, and the Classic
games share a UI codebase whose `AlertFrame` anchors and stacks alerts exactly the way
retail's does, with the same 276×96 loot toast, the same options panel API and the same
minimap. All of that was checked against Blizzard's UI source for each game's current
build. Forever restricts what addons can read about combat, which does not affect an addon
that never reads any.

What differs is how much Blizzard sends through that frame:

- **Retail and Forever** — loot, achievements and the other alerts listed in
  [the CurseForge description](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/blob/main/docs/curseforge-description.md#what-it-moves).
- **The Classic games** — loot never goes through it, so what moves is mostly achievement
  toasts, in the games that have achievements. Classic Era has none, so very little appears
  there at all.

`/ltm test` fires a genuine loot toast in every game, so placement can always be checked.
The Addon Compartment is the one feature that is not everywhere: only retail and Forever
have one, and the Classic games ignore its TOC fields.

Wrath of the Lich King Classic and Cataclysm Classic are not listed because neither is
running any more: those realms moved on to Cataclysm Classic and then to Mists of Pandaria
Classic.

Patch 12.0 raised the floor for mainline addons to `120000`, so the retail number has to be
kept current, and the others have to track their clients the same way. Check the live value
in any game with `/dump select(4, GetBuildInfo())`.

## Translations

The addon's own text follows the game client's language. That covers the anchor box, the
tooltips, the options panel and the chat messages. Besides English it has German, French,
Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. The
Latin American Spanish client shares the Spanish text, and the European Portuguese client
shares the Brazilian Portuguese text. The one-line description in the in-game addon list is
translated as well.

Slash commands and the addon's name stay in English in every language. WoW commands are
typed in English in every client, and it keeps them the same in guides and bug reports.

The translations in this repository are first drafts, not written by native speakers.
Translators can improve them through the project's translation tool on CurseForge, and
corrections are also welcome as a GitHub issue or pull request.

Every string lives in [`Locales.lua`](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/blob/main/Locales.lua): English first, then one table per
language. A language that leaves a string out falls back to English, so a gap shows English
rather than a blank. The tests still require every language to be complete, and every
translation to keep its `%s` placeholders and its slash commands. Adding a string therefore
means adding it in every language at the same time. No string contains a line break: the
anchor box's two lines are two strings, which the code joins.

### How CurseForge translations reach players

`Locales.lua` ends with one packager line per CurseForge language:

```lua
do local L = translations.deDE --@localization(locale="deDE", format="lua_additive_table", handle-unlocalized="ignore")@
end
```

In a copy from git that line is only a comment, so the drafts stand alone. When a release is
packaged, the BigWigs packager replaces it with that language's translations from CurseForge,
which are assigned over the drafts. Anything nobody has translated there is left out, so the
draft stays. Latin American Spanish starts from the Spanish, CurseForge's improvements
included, and then takes anything translated for it specifically.

The release workflow makes that safe:

1. It sends the English text to CurseForge (`tools/upload_translations.sh english`). This
   uses CurseForge's `DeletePhrase` mode, so CurseForge always holds exactly the addon's
   phrases: a new string reaches translators, and a removed one disappears there too.
2. It packages the addon once without publishing, and runs the whole test suite against
   that package. Translators' work never passes through this repository, so this is where
   it gets checked. A translation that drops a `%s` or rewrites a slash command fails the
   release before anything is tagged, and the failing check names the language and string to
   fix on CurseForge.
3. Only then does it tag and publish.

To give translators the drafts to start from, run the **Translations** workflow once with
**drafts**. It uploads the English, then each language's drafts, and finishes with the same
package-and-test check a release makes, without publishing anything, which confirms the round
trip works before a release depends on it. Don't run it with **drafts** again after
translators have started: uploading a draft replaces whatever CurseForge holds for that
phrase, their work included. The **english** option only sends the English, which every
release does anyway.

`tools/export_locale.lua <locale>` prints any language's strings in the form CurseForge
imports. Both scripts need the `CF_API_KEY` secret the release already uses.

## Saved variables

`LootToastMoverDB` is account-wide and holds the anchor's screen position, the minimap
button's placement under `minimapButton`, `growDown` for the stacking direction, and a
`schema` number used for upgrades. `/ltm reset` clears the position keys.

The table is checked once, when the addon loads. A position the game could not use (an
anchor point that is not one, an offset that is not a number) is dropped and the box goes
back to its default, rather than raising an error at every login.

Two upgrades happen automatically on first load:

- **From 4.8.x**: the stale `minimap` sub-table left behind by the old LibDBIcon button is
  dropped.
- **From 4.9.x**: saved positions are shifted so toasts stay exactly where you put them.
  Older versions drew the first toast 31 pixels *below* a 60-pixel box; the box is now the
  toast's real 96-pixel footprint with the toast sitting on it, so the stored offset has to
  move to compensate. The shift depends on which anchor point was saved.

## Dependencies

None, still. Versions up to 4.8.x bundled LibStub, CallbackHandler-1.0, LibDataBroker-1.1
and LibDBIcon-1.0 — roughly 930 lines of third-party code — purely for a minimap button and
a broker plugin. Both are back without any of it:

- The **minimap button** is written directly against the widget API, about sixty lines in
  `LootToastMover.lua`.
- The **broker plugin** looks LibDataBroker up with `LibStub:GetLibrary("LibDataBroker-1.1",
  true)` instead of shipping it. Every broker display embeds the library itself, so it is
  always loaded whenever there is a bar for the plugin to appear on; with no bar installed
  the lookup returns nil and the addon carries on. Registration happens once at
  `PLAYER_LOGIN`, after every addon has loaded — there is no retry ticker.

## Development

The repository root *is* the addon, which is the layout the
[BigWigs packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager) expects. `.pkgmeta` renames it
to `LootToastMover` when building the zip.

Checks, all of which CI runs on every push:

```sh
luacheck .                    # lint
lua5.1 tests/run_tests.lua    # regression tests against a stubbed WoW API
lua5.1 tests/check_toc.lua    # TOC and packaging sanity (see below)
```

One more runs weekly instead, because it depends on Blizzard and not on this repository:

```sh
tools/check_blizzard_source.sh                        # retail
WOW_GAME=classic_era tools/check_blizzard_source.sh   # any other game, by mirror branch
```

It reads Blizzard's UI source for one game and checks each fact the addon rests on: how
alerts are anchored and stacked, the loot toast's 276×96 size, the Edit Mode events, the
list Escape closes. The **Blizzard source check** workflow runs it for all six games every
week and opens an issue naming what changed. It publishes nothing.

### If something goes wrong in game

Everything the game calls in the addon is wrapped. An error is passed to the game's error
handler, so BugSack and similar addons record it, and is mentioned in chat once. After
three in a session the addon stops reacting to Blizzard's alert layout until a `/reload`;
slash commands and the options panel keep working. Saved settings are not touched.

WoW runs Lua 5.1, so the tooling does too. See [tests/README.md](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/blob/main/tests/README.md) for how
the stub works and what each test guards against.

## Releasing

Publishing is **manual**. Nothing fires on a schedule — the addon has real users, and an
unattended upload is not something that should happen while nobody is watching.

Run the **Release** workflow from the Actions tab and pick a bump:

| Bump | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | Tag and publish what is already committed, version unchanged |
| `patch` | 4.11.1 → 4.11.2 |
| `minor` | 4.11.1 → 4.12.0 |
| `major` | 4.11.1 → 5.0.0 |

It bumps `## Version` in the TOC, the banner in `LootToastMover.lua` and `CHANGELOG.md`
together and runs the tests. It sends the English text to CurseForge's translation tool, then
packages the addon with CurseForge's translations in it and tests that package (see
[Translations](#translations)). Only then does it commit, tag, and publish to CurseForge
(project `1262382`) and GitHub releases. The optional **notes** input becomes the changelog
line. Nothing ships if any test fails, and it refuses to reuse an existing tag.

Pushing a `v*` tag by hand also works and just packages that tag.

### When a game patch lands

Tick **update_interface** on a release run. It pulls the current Interface version of every
supported game into the TOC as part of that release, so nobody has to look six numbers up.
With no **notes**, the changelog line names every game's version.

Being an expansion behind is what took this addon out of service once already — a 12.x
client will not load anything below Interface `120000`, and 4.8.3 sat on 11.1.5 for months
— but noticing that and shipping to players are separate decisions, and this keeps the
second one deliberate. A run that updates the Interface version needs a real bump, not
`none`, or there is no new version for anyone to update to; the workflow says so and stops.

It tracks live clients only. A beta or PTR Interface number would mark the addon out of
date on the live client it is meant to support. Forever is the exception until it launches,
because its beta is the only Forever client there is: for now the updater reads Forever's
number from Blizzard's `wow_classic_beta` product. If any lookup returns another game's
build, or nothing at all, `tests/check_toc.lua` fails the run before anything is tagged or
published.

The workflow names the games the way the updater does — `retail`, `forever`, `mists`,
`titan`, `anniversary` and `vanilla` — and `vanilla` is not interchangeable with
`classic_era`. The updater checks for `classic` first, so `classic_era` quietly fetches
Mists of Pandaria Classic a second time and leaves Classic Era out.

When Blizzard moves a Classic game on to its next expansion, the new Interface number falls
outside every range in `tools/games.lua`, and the check fails on purpose. Try the addon in
that client, then add the game to `tools/games.lua` and the workflow's flavor list, and
update this README and the CurseForge description.

`tools/bump_version.lua <none|patch|minor|major> [note]` does the file edits and can be run
by hand; it prints the resulting version.

Bumping and publishing live in one job deliberately. Pushing a tag from a workflow does not
start another workflow, because GitHub does not trigger runs from events made with
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, so a job that only tagged would appear to succeed and publish nothing.

Publishing requires one repository secret, `CF_API_KEY`, holding a CurseForge API token
(Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions). `GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided automatically.

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/SteveWeed79/loot-toast-mover/blob/main/LICENSE). The addon ships the licence file inside the zip, and declares it in the
TOC as `## X-License: MIT`.

# Changelog

Notable changes to LootToastMover. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## [4.16.0] - 2026-11-19

### Added

- **Stack new toasts downward.** A new checkbox in the options panel. Toasts normally stack
  upward from the anchor box, which runs a burst of them off the screen when the box is near
  the top. Tick it and the first toast still lands on the box, and the rest hang below it.
  Off by default, so nothing changes unless you ask.
- **The anchor box appears in Edit Mode.** It shows when you open Edit Mode and goes when you
  close it, alongside the rest of your UI. A box you had already shown is left alone.
- **Escape hides the anchor box**, and showing it with `/ltm` or a click now says in chat how
  to hide it again.
- A bug-report form on GitHub.

### Changed

- **A new install starts without the minimap button in retail and Forever**, where the addon
  is already listed in the Addon Compartment next to the minimap. `/ltm minimap` or the
  options panel brings it back. If you already have the addon, your button stays as it is,
  and the Classic games, which have no compartment, still show it.

### Fixed

- A damaged saved position no longer causes an error at every login. The box goes back to
  its default position instead, and the rest of the addon still loads.
- An error inside the addon is now caught, mentioned once in chat and passed to your error
  addon, instead of interrupting Blizzard's alert code. After three in one session the addon
  stops reacting to new toasts until you `/reload`.

## [4.15.1] - 2026-10-13

### Changed

- **Updated for patch 12.1.5**, so the game does not flag the addon as out of date. Regions
  that patch later in the week keep loading it on 12.1.0 until they update.

## [4.15.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **Help translate LootToastMover.** Any translation can now be improved on CurseForge,
  through the project's Localization page, and every release includes what translators have
  written there. Until someone improves a string, you see the same translation as before.

### Changed

- The text on the anchor box now breaks after "Drag me." in every language, instead of in
  the middle of the second sentence.

## [4.14.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **LootToastMover now speaks your language.** The anchor box, the tooltips, the options
  panel and the chat messages follow your game client's language: German, French, Spanish,
  Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese, as well as
  English. The description in the in-game addon list is translated too, and the options
  panel's buttons widen to fit a longer translation.
- Slash commands stay the same in every language, so `/ltm test` and the rest work exactly
  as before.
- These translations are first drafts, not written by native speakers. If something reads
  awkwardly in your language, suggest a better wording on GitHub.

## [4.13.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **Now loads in every version of World of Warcraft that Blizzard runs.** Alongside retail
  and Forever, the same download now covers Mists of Pandaria Classic, Classic Era,
  TBC Anniversary and Titan Reforged Classic. The anchor box, `/ltm test`, the minimap
  button, the options panel and the broker plugin all work the same in each of them, and
  nothing changes for retail or Forever players.
- The Classic games send far fewer alerts through the frame this addon moves. Loot never
  goes through it there, so what the anchor moves is mostly achievement toasts, in the
  games that have achievements. Classic Era has none, so very little appears there at all.
  `/ltm test` fires a real loot toast in every game, so you can always check the position.
- The Addon Compartment only exists in retail and Forever. In the Classic games, use the
  minimap button, the options panel or `/ltm`.

## [4.12.0] - 2026-10-02

### Added

- **Now also loads in World of Warcraft: Forever.** One download covers both games. Forever
  runs on the retail game client, so the addon itself needed no changes to work there: the
  anchor box, `/ltm test`, the minimap button, the options panel, the broker plugin and the
  Addon Compartment are all the same as in retail. Nothing changes for retail players.
- Installing by hand for the Forever beta? The folder is
  `World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/`.

## [4.11.2] - 2026-09-15

### Fixed

- **Opening the options panel threw a Lua error instead of opening anything.** Every route
  in was affected: right-clicking the minimap button, right-clicking the broker plugin,
  right-clicking the Addon Compartment entry, and `/ltm config`. The options panel itself
  was fine and always had been — nothing could reach it. Introduced in 4.11.0.
- If a future game patch changes that call again, the addon now says so in chat rather than
  throwing an error popup, and the slash commands keep working.

## [4.11.1] - 2026-09-14

### Changed

- LootToastMover is now explicitly MIT licensed, and the licence ships with the addon.

## [4.11.0] - 2026-09-13

**You can actually find the addon now.** 4.9.0 left Blizzard's Addon Compartment as the
only way in, which meant an installed addon looked like a missing one. Three ways back,
and still with no bundled libraries.

### Added

- **The minimap button is back** — the bag icon on the minimap ring. Left-click shows or
  hides the anchor box, right-click opens the options panel, and you can drag it anywhere
  around the ring. Hide it from the options panel or with `/ltm minimap`.
- **An options panel**, under Game Menu → Options → AddOns → LootToastMover, with buttons
  for everything the slash commands do. `/ltm config` opens it directly.
- **The broker plugin is back.** If you use Titan Panel, Bazooka, ChocolateBar, ElvUI
  datatexts or any other broker display, LootToastMover appears in its plugin list again.
  This was removed in 4.9.0 along with the libraries and should not have been.
- `/ltm` as a short alias for `/loottoastpos`, plus `/ltm config` and `/ltm minimap`.

### Changed

- The minimap button is written against the game's own widget API rather than LibDBIcon,
  and the broker plugin uses the LibDataBroker your broker display already loads, so the
  addon is still a single file with no third-party dependencies.

## [4.10.0] - 2026-09-12

### Added

- `/loottoastpos test` shows a sample loot toast, so you can check placement without
  waiting for a drop.

### Changed

- **The anchor box is now the real thing.** It matches the exact size of a loot toast
  (276×96) and sits exactly where the first toast will appear, with later toasts stacking
  upward from it. Previously the box was a 260×60 placeholder and the first toast actually
  landed 31 pixels *below* it, so what you dragged was not where toasts went.
- Your saved position is adjusted automatically the first time you log in, so toasts stay
  exactly where you had them. Nothing to redo.

## [4.9.0] - 2026-09-12

### Changed

- The minimap button is replaced by Blizzard's **Addon Compartment** — the addon-list
  button next to the minimap. Click the LootToastMover entry there to show or hide the
  anchor box, as before.

### Removed

- All four bundled libraries: LibStub, CallbackHandler-1.0, LibDataBroker-1.1 and
  LibDBIcon-1.0. They were carried solely to provide the minimap button, which the game
  now does natively. The addon is a single Lua file with no third-party dependencies.
- The unused `minimap` entry the old button left behind in your saved variables is cleared
  when you upgrade.

**If you use a broker display** such as Titan Panel or ChocolateBar, LootToastMover no
longer appears in it, because the LibDataBroker object went with the libraries. Use the
Addon Compartment or `/loottoastpos` instead.

## [4.8.4] - 2026-09-11

### Fixed
